proposed.sourceName: South African National Halaal Authority (SANHA) — E570 (Stearic Acid)
proposed.paraphrase: SANHA classifies E570 (stearic acid) as Mushbooh (doubtful): it may come from animal or vegetable oils (or synthetically from vegetable oils), so the source must be verified — plant-derived is halal, animal-derived only if the animal was slaughtered Islamically.

proposed.sourceName: SeekersGuidance — 'Is It Permissible to Use Products That Contain Stearic Acid?' (Ustadh Salman Younas)
proposed.paraphrase: A Hanafi answer holding that products containing stearic acid are permissible even if the source could be animal (including non-halal), because it has undergone an essential chemical change (istihalat al-'ayn); it adds that using a product from only permissible sources remains superior — the permissive side of the dispute.

researcherNote: E570 seeded lenient grade 3 (contested) — kept contested: SeekersGuidance permits via istihalah but SANHA mushbooh + possible pork/non-zabiha animal source keeps it doubtful. Two independent tier-1. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01 (batch pre-approval).
